# Daniel Heene's Personal Website

> Source for [daniel.heene.io](https://daniel.heene.io): a personal website, blog, and resume
> builder built on Next.js 16 (App Router, React 19) and Payload CMS 3.x, with MongoDB, Redis,
> and S3-compatible storage.

This is a code repository, not a documentation site — the files below are the entry points an
AI coding agent should read before making changes, not end-user docs. `AGENTS.md` is the most
important file: read it first, every time.

## Start Here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): Required reading before any change — stack, code style, architecture
  notes, and known security guardrails (public SSE channels remain unauthenticated by design,
  raw SVG is sanitized server-side before rendering, `CRON_SECRET` is declared but unenforced).
- [README.md](README.md): Setup and local development — Doppler-based env config, Docker
  services, available scripts, project structure, testing, CI/deployment.

## Configuration

- [payload.config.ts](payload.config.ts): Payload CMS configuration (collections, globals,
  plugins, S3 storage, KV cache) — repo root, not under `src/`.
- [next.config.ts](next.config.ts): Next.js configuration; validates the environment against
  the Zod schema at startup and owns the opt-in dev tunnel. There is no `env:` block: browser
  values are plain `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variables.
- [proxy.ts](proxy.ts): Next.js 16 request proxy (the former `middleware.ts`); canonicalizes blog
  listing URLs.
- [src/types/environment.ts](src/types/environment.ts): Zod schema and source of truth for all
  environment variables; validated at process start.
- [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml): Local infrastructure (MongoDB, Redis, S3-compatible
  storage) — the app itself runs via `bun run dev`, not as a compose service.
- [oxlint.config.ts](oxlint.config.ts), [oxfmt.config.ts](oxfmt.config.ts): Linting/formatting rules (Oxc toolchain, not ESLint/Prettier).
- [vitest.config.ts](vitest.config.ts) / [vitest.setup.ts](vitest.setup.ts): Unit test config
  and shared mocks (`payload`, `next/cache`, `redis`).
- [playwright.config.ts](playwright.config.ts): E2E test config (Chromium).
- [commitlint.config.mjs](commitlint.config.mjs): Conventional Commits enforcement.

## Source Layout

- [app/](app): Next.js App Router — `(frontend)` for the public site and its route handlers
  (preview, sse, health, icons/collection, the blog RSS feed, the resume download), `(payload)`
  for the admin panel and Payload's REST API, `llms.txt/` for the site's public `/llms.txt`.
- [src/collections/](src/collections): Payload Collections (Media*, Pages, BlogPosts,
  BlogTopics, Resume*, Redirects, References, Users).
- [src/globals/](src/globals): Payload Globals (SiteSettings, PDFGeneratorSettings, etc.).
- [src/blocks/](src/blocks): Reusable Payload Blocks (resume sections, content blocks).
- [src/fields/](src/fields): Custom/reusable Payload field factories.
- [src/lib/access/](src/lib/access): Access control functions — no role system; any
  authenticated Payload user is fully trusted.
- [src/components/](src/components): React components.
- [src/lib/](src/lib): Framework-agnostic utilities, including `RedisHandler.ts` (cache +
  pub/sub for SSE) and `lib/seed/` (shared seed/clean logic for fixture data, used by both
  CLI scripts and the admin panel).
- [src/emails/](src/emails): React Email templates and rendering (contact form notifications).
- [src/pdf/](src/pdf): PDF generation (resume export).
- [src/jobs-queue/](src/jobs-queue): Payload Jobs Queue task/workflow configs plus their
  handlers (`handlers/`), which only the standalone worker (`scripts/start-worker.mjs`) runs.
- [src/plugins/](src/plugins): Local Payload plugins (redirects, references).
- [src/widgets/](src/widgets): Custom Payload dashboard widgets (async server components registered
  in `payload.config.ts`; client parts call server actions from `src/lib/actions/`).
- [src/lib/actions/](src/lib/actions): Server actions (`'use server'`) for admin mutations (job
  rescheduling, cancellation, etc.).
- [e2e/](e2e): Playwright E2E specs — structural smoke tests, not content assertions.
